review_comments: You might want to see https://github.com/systemd/systemd/issues/17575 and https://github.com/systemd/systemd/pull/18010

Well, this changes only `systemctl --when=`, i.e. our new-ish stuff rather than the sysv-compat `shutdown`. _Maybe_ the behavior was sensible for the latter, whose time spec is restricted within 24 hours, but not here. Therefore I really think the new logic is the way to go.

I mean, I introduced `--when=` originally, and I nowadays strongly feel like that it was a mistake to take this fallback logic from sysv compat code. I'd also add support for `sleep --when=` in the future, and it seems like a good time to first get rid of such problematic behavior from systemctl.

cc @poettering
hmm, you changed this now, but that means we'll no reboot at all if no maintenance time is configured, right?
and is that desirable? i woudl assume that in many cases "reboot now or posibly delay to maintenance window if one is defined" is the policy people want. no?
Nope. Previously `EOPNOTSUPP` was used to _disable_ fallback logic in systemctl. So none of the commits change the behavior regarding unset designated maintenance window
